thread:
maria: Hey team — kicking off networking bring-up for the new chi cluster tomorrow. Need routing, peering/TGW decisions, NAT/egress plan, and DNS zone handoff. Who's free for a quick runbook sync?

devon: I can take routing + route table validation. Quick notes: we should avoid per-AZ NAT gateways if we can centralize egress to the TGW egress VPC to save cost.

liam: +1 on central egress. But remember TGW attachment charges might offset NAT savings depending on traffic patterns. We should run a cost estimate with projected egress GB/month.

aj_ops: I can own peering/TGW config and the automation bits (Terraform). Will need the CIDR ranges for chi cluster and the core-transport VPC. Also: do we want cross-account TGW attachments or account-scoped?

maria: Core-transport VPC CIDR is 10.10.0.0/16 (account infra-core). Chi cluster will be 10.40.0.0/16 (account infra-chi). Cross-account TGW attachment preferred for centralized egress and monitoring.

devon: Draft runbook sketch below — please call out gaps.

--- RUNBOOK DRAFT ---
1) Bootstrap network objects (infra-chi):
   - Create VPC 10.40.0.0/16, subnets per AZ (public/private), ensure correct tags (redwood:region=chi).
   - Create private route tables for worker subnets.

2) TGW / Peering decision:
   - Create TGW in infra-core account.
   - Create cross-account attachment from infra-chi to TGW.
   - Create route table on TGW: propagate attachments and add route to egress VPC (10.20.0.0/16).
   - Rationale: central egress + observability + consistent ACLs.

3) Route propagation / prefix lists:
   - Use prefix-lists for cluster CIDRs and onprem CIDRs.
   - On infra-chi, add route in private RTs: 0.0.0.0/0 -> TGW for controlled egress, and specific routes to other infra VPCs.

4) NAT/Egress choices:
   - Preferred: NAT egress through central egress VPC via TGW with centralized NAT Gateway(s) (one per AZ for HA).
   - If cost-prohibitive: fallback to NAT instances in infra-chi with autoscaling + monitoring.
   - Note: central egress implies SNAT IPs come from egress VPC elastic IP pool — ensure allocation and ACLs.

5) DNS zones & delegation:
   - Create hosted zone chi.redwood.internal in Route53 (private hosted zone).
   - Delegate chi subdomain from infra-core via VPC association with infra-chi and infra-core VPCs.
   - Add A records for control-plane endpoints and internal LB CNAMEs.

6) Validation steps:
   - From a worker in private subnet:
     - curl -v http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ to verify metadata access.
     - curl -v --resolve "service.internal:443:10.20.5.12" https://service.internal/health to ensure cross-VPC routing and DNS resolution.
     - traceroute to 8.8.8.8 to confirm egress path via TGW -> egress NAT.
   - Route table checks: aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=<vpc-chi>
   - Route53 check: dig @<resolver-ip> service.chi.redwood.internal +short

7) Handoff:
   - Infra-chi owner creates GH ticket with terraform plan URL, egress IPs listed, and test results.
   - Tag cluster networking as "ready" and notify infra-oncall for 48h watch.

--- END RUNBOOK ---

liam: For validation add: curl --interface eth0 -I http://ifconfig.co to verify NAT IP, and also confirm -n for no DNS cache.

aj_ops: Terraform notes — we'll use module: modules/tgw-attachment with variables: remote_account_id, vpc_id, attachment_subnets. Also include acceptance test that posts to internal healthcheck and checks 200.

maria: Security ask: need to ensure no routes leak to prod VPCs. Add route table deny checks and prefix-list enforcement. Also ensure security groups on LBs only allow TGW source prefix-list.

devon: Good call. Add a post-provision automated smoke: run quick e2e that launches a small pod that does: dig _etcd._tcp.cluster.local SRV and curl a control-plane endpoint. If fails, rollback TGW attachment.

infra-oncall: I'll schedule the 48h watch and add monitoring dashboards: TGW bytes, NAT gateway bytes, route table anomalies, and CloudWatch alarms for route propagation failures.

netbot: deployment-bot: TGW attachment created by aj_ops from infra-chi -> tgw-0a1b2c3d; status: pending acceptance.

aj_ops: Accepted. Applied terraform plan with expect changes. Pushing plan URL: https://ci.internal/plan/6578

maria: Quick Q: For DNS, do we want split-horizon so public-facing services still resolve via public hosted zone?

devon: Yes — private hosted zone only for internal names. Public names continue to live in the public zone. Make sure internal LB CNAMEs point to private zone records.

liam: Cost note: we'll prototype with central NAT gateways but if egress > 200TB/month per region, re-evaluate for localized NAT or using third-party egress appliances.

aj_ops: Action items assigned:
 - aj_ops: create TF module + PR for TGW attachment and route propagation (ETA: EOD).
 - devon: write route table & prefix-list validation scripts + smoke e2e (ETA: tomorrow morning).
 - liam: run cost calc for TGW vs per-AZ NAT (ETA: afternoon).
 - maria: prepare DNS delegation ticket and update internal docs (ETA: EOD).
 - infra-oncall: enable watch and dashboards (ETA: before handoff).

maria: Thanks all. We'll run the handoff once infra-oncall confirms dashboards. If anyone hits permissions issues for cross-account attachments ping me and I'll escalate with security. :thumbsup:
